subject: Nonstandard hosting ops & AZ resourcing sync
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: ops@bluehaven.io, cloud-cto@greenbank.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 29 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Nonstandard hosting ops & AZ resourcing sync

Hi all,

Per our contract kickoff, BlueHaven has flagged a requirement for private VPC deployments across two AZs with strict isolation and a lower-latency on-prem fallback for disaster-recovery. I want to pull together a short cross-functional decision sync to align on architecture assumptions and the minimal staffing runway needed to support an initial pilot (2 clusters, 3 months).

Asks:
- Architecture: Karthik, can you confirm whether our current private packaging supports dual-AZ active/passive + on-prem failover without a full rework? I sketched a failure-mode diagram and attached it (az-failure-mode-diagram.png).
- Ops/resourcing: Kimberly, what is the minimal oncall and runbook scope we need to guarantee a 99.5% pilot SLO for token-serving endpoints? The attached spreadsheet (runway_staffing-v2.xlsx) has two staffing options — please mark gaps.
- Timeline & rollout: Marcus, can you propose a short window for a canary pilot (preferred Q3 start) and any key gating infra tasks?

BlueHaven (ops@bluehaven.io), please confirm any network constraints we should assume (private peering, no internet egress from the enclave, KMS placement).

I propose a 30-minute sync Monday 9:30am PT to walk the diagram and staffing options. If that works, I’ll send a calendar invite and include the brief.

Thanks,
Chloe
Chloe Martin
Program Manager, Product Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachments: runway_staffing-v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), az-failure-mode-diagram.png (image)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, ops@bluehaven.io, cloud-cto@greenbank.com
Date: Fri, 29 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Nonstandard hosting ops & AZ resourcing sync

Chloe —

Thanks for the kickoff. Quick read of the diagram: the packaging we ship today supports multi-AZ where traffic is routed through a regional gateway and model shards are colocated on private subnets. That covers active/passive within a cloud provider. The on-prem fallback is the trick: we can do a lightweight on-prem appliance that pulls pinned model artifacts and KV snapshotting, but it requires:

- Manual bootstrap of model weights (sideload/secure transfer) for the first pilot (no automated multi-site sync yet).
- An ops runbook for KV cache reconciliation after failover — we don’t have an automated log-shipping path in place.
- An initial compatibility test matrix for the customer's on-prem GPU types (we only test our quantized pipelines on Ampere and Hopper families).

If BlueHaven can accept a manual bootstrap for the pilot and a documented failover checklist, we avoid a 6–8 week engineering effort to build an automated cross-site model sync.

Questions for BlueHaven: what GPU families will be available on the on-prem appliance? Also, confirm whether the customer requires KMS/HSM in their VPC or if a customer-managed KMS outside the enclave is acceptable.

I’ll be on the sync Monday.

—Karthik
Principal Architect, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@bluehaven.io
Date: Fri, 29 Jun 2028 13:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Nonstandard hosting ops & AZ resourcing sync

Chloe/Karthik —

I reviewed the runway spreadsheet and sketched two viable staffing models:

Option A (Lean pilot):
- 1x SRE oncall (primary) with 1x backup (on-call rotation, 24/7 coverage via shared pool)
- 0.5 FTE Program lead (part-time) for customer coordination
- 1x Solutions Engineer for bootstrap and initial KMS setup (short-term block)
Estimated burn: ~3 weeks of full-time SE work + ongoing 0.5 FTE during pilot.

Option B (Conservative):
- 2x SREs (dedicated) for triage and runbook maturation
- 1x Customer Reliability Engineer embedded (3 months)
- 1x Security reviewer on rotational audits
Estimated burn: ~1.0 FTE ops + 1.5 FTE SE over the pilot window.

Notes / blockers:
- Our current runbooks do not include KV reconciliation steps for cross-site handoff. If we treat the on-prem as ‘read-only passive’ until a full rebuild, we can simplify the runbook and reduce staffing.
- We need a signed exception for manual artifact transfer; security is okay with it for a timeboxed pilot but wants a documented checklist and audit log (DocuSign or S3 transfer record).

I flagged the specific gaps in the attached spreadsheet (column: RUNBOOK_GAPS). Happy to go through rows in the call.

Kimberly
Director, Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: BlueHaven Ops <ops@bluehaven.io>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 30 Jun 2028 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Nonstandard hosting ops & AZ resourcing sync

Chloe / team —

Thanks for the detail and the two staffing options. A few clarifications from our side:

- On-prem hardware: we plan to provision A100 (40GB) nodes for the fallback appliance. We can confirm serials/firmware next week.
- KMS: for compliance we need an HSM-backed KMS in our VPC; we cannot allow a KMS outside the enclave.
- Network: private peering only, no outbound egress from the enclave.

We are comfortable with the manual bootstrap approach for a 3-month pilot provided:
- We have an explicit runbook and audit of artifact transfer;
- Redwood provides an on-call contact during business hours and an escalation path for P1s outside of that window.

We can do the Monday 9:30am PT sync. Please include any network CIDR and port requirements in the calendar invite.

—Samir Patel
Head of Infrastructure
BlueHaven Health
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@bluehaven.io
Date: Sat, 30 Jun 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Nonstandard hosting ops & AZ resourcing sync

Quick summary ahead of the sync:

Decisions to make Monday (short list):
1) Accept manual bootstrap for pilot (yes/no) — reduces dev time but increases ops coordination.
2) Confirm HSM-in-VPC requirement — if yes, engineering must validate KMS integration and key rotation with customer.
3) Pick staffing model A vs B — Kimberly to recommend final.
4) Canary window request: target week of Aug 14 for internal canary, external pilot start Aug 28.

Action items I’ll take before the meeting: calendar invite + CIDR/port list; an initial runbook stub in the Drive link; and a delta checklist for security exception (DocuSign link placeholder in the Drive doc).

If we can land on manual bootstrap + option A for pilot governance, we can accelerate to the proposed canary window with only minor engineering gating tasks (compatibility smoke tests and KMS integration).

Marcus Lin
Head of Product Delivery
Redwood Inference
